slides.title: Larmor gyromotion: the fundamental orbit
slides.body:
**Lorentz force**: F = q(E + v × B). In a uniform B with no E, a charged particle executes a **helical orbit** — circular motion in the plane perpendicular to B (gyromotion), uniform along B.

**Cyclotron / gyrofrequency**:
$$\omega_c = \frac{|q|B}{m}, \quad f_c = \frac{\omega_c}{2\pi}$$

Electron cyclotron: f_{ce}[Hz] ≈ 28 × B[Gauss] × 10⁹ — so at B = 5 T tokamak field, f_{ce} ≈ 140 GHz (microwave heating uses ECRH at this frequency).

**Larmor (gyro) radius**:
$$r_L = \frac{m v_\perp}{|q| B}$$

This is the perpendicular orbit radius. Key examples:
- **Tokamak ions** (1 keV D⁺, B=5 T): r_L,i ~ 0.6 mm.
- **Tokamak electrons** (1 keV, B=5 T): r_L,e ~ 0.01 mm (60× smaller because m_e/m_p ~ 1/1836 + factor √m).
- **Fast alpha particles** (3.5 MeV He²⁺ in ITER, B=5.3 T): r_L ~ 5.5 cm — significant fraction of minor radius!
- **Solar wind protons** (~1 keV, B~5 nT at 1 AU): r_L ~ 100 km.
- **Earth magnetosphere ring-current ions** (~50 keV, B~30 nT): r_L ~ 700 km.
- **Cosmic-ray protons** (1 GeV, ISM B~1 μG): r_L ~ AU; (10²⁰ eV cosmic rays): r_L ~ 100 kpc — galaxy can't confine them (Hillas criterion for cosmic-ray origins).

**Pitch angle**: tan α = v⊥/v∥. Particles with low pitch angle (mostly parallel) escape mirrors easily; high pitch angle (mostly perpendicular) are trapped.

**Guiding center**: average position of the gyrating particle — the slow motion of the guiding center is what drift theory describes.

**Magnetization** holds when r_L ≪ scale of B variation (L_B = |B/∇B|): then a particle 'sees' a locally uniform B + drift theory applies. Failure of this assumption → finite-Larmor-radius (FLR) corrections + gyrokinetic theory.

slides.title: Drifts of the guiding center
slides.body:
Add a slowly-varying second force/field on top of B → the guiding center **drifts** perpendicular to both. The general drift formula for a force F:
$$\mathbf{v}_d = \frac{\mathbf{F} \times \mathbf{B}}{q B^2}$$

**E × B drift** (most important!):
$$\mathbf{v}_E = \frac{\mathbf{E} \times \mathbf{B}}{B^2}$$

**Charge-independent + mass-independent** — electrons + ions drift together, no current. Magnitude E[V/m] / B[T] in m/s. Drives **plasma rotation** in tokamaks, **ionospheric convection**, **solar-wind interaction** with magnetospheres. The basis of **Hall thrusters** for spacecraft propulsion.

**Grad-B drift** (gradient drift):
$$\mathbf{v}_{\nabla B} = \frac{m v_\perp^2}{2 q B^3}(\mathbf{B} \times \nabla B)$$

Depends on charge sign → drives **current**. Comes from r_L being smaller in stronger-field regions of the orbit.

**Curvature drift** (in curved field lines with radius R_c):
$$\mathbf{v}_R = \frac{m v_\parallel^2}{q B^2}\frac{\mathbf{R}_c \times \mathbf{B}}{R_c^2}$$

Also charge-dependent. In tokamaks the grad-B + curvature drifts together drive vertical charge separation → vertical E-field → outward E×B drift → unstable! Solved by the **rotational transform** (poloidal field) which short-circuits the charge separation.

**Polarization drift** (time-varying E):
$$\mathbf{v}_p = \frac{m}{q B^2}\frac{d\mathbf{E}_\perp}{dt}$$

Mass-dependent → ion polarization drift ≫ electron → drives **polarization current** central to MHD inertia + lower-hybrid waves.

**Gravitational drift**: v_g = (m/q)(g × B)/B². Tiny for fusion but important in **stellar plasmas + Earth's magnetosphere** (drives equatorial electrojet).

**Diamagnetic drift** (fluid-only, no individual particle equivalent): v_d = -∇p × B/(nqB²) — appears in fluid description as collective effect of pressure gradient + finite r_L.

slides.title: Adiabatic invariants + magnetic mirrors
slides.body:
**Adiabatic invariants**: quantities conserved when the field varies slowly compared to the motion. Plasma has three classical invariants associated with the three periodicities of trapped-particle motion.

**First invariant — magnetic moment μ**:
$$\mu = \frac{m v_\perp^2}{2 B}$$

Conserved when (∂B/∂t)/(ω_c B) ≪ 1 + spatial variation r_L|∇B|/B ≪ 1. Physical: magnetic flux through Larmor orbit. Conservation makes the particle act as a **little magnetic dipole**.

Consequence: as a particle moves into stronger B (with energy conserved), v⊥² ∝ B grows → v∥² shrinks → particle slows + reverses. This is **magnetic mirroring**.

**Loss cone** (mirror machine):
$$\sin^2\theta_{lc} = \frac{B_{min}}{B_{max}} = \frac{1}{R_m}$$

R_m = mirror ratio. Particles with pitch angle below θ_lc escape; otherwise trapped. **Mirror confinement** by itself is leaky (open field lines, ~constant loss-cone) — limited fusion utility (LLNL MFTF-B canceled 1986); but mirrors do confine planetary radiation belts spectacularly.

**Second invariant — longitudinal action J**:
$$J = \oint m v_\parallel \, ds$$

Conserved over a full bounce between mirror points. Governs **bounce motion** of trapped particles + how they drift in azimuthal direction.

**Third invariant — flux Φ**:
$$\Phi = \oint \mathbf{A} \cdot d\boldsymbol{\ell}$$

Magnetic flux enclosed by full drift orbit around the system. Conserved over the slow azimuthal drift. Broken by storm-time field changes → radial diffusion of radiation belt particles.

**Van Allen radiation belts** (James Van Allen, **Explorer 1, 1958** — first US satellite + first major space discovery!): inner belt (protons ~10-100 MeV) + outer belt (electrons ~MeV) trapped by Earth's dipole field via μ + J + Φ conservation. Particles **bounce** between magnetic mirrors near the poles (period ~seconds) + **drift** azimuthally (ions westward, electrons eastward — the **ring current** that depresses Earth's surface field during magnetic storms; period ~minutes).

**Loss cone + auroras**: pitch-angle scattering by VLF waves + whistlers pushes particles into the loss cone, where they precipitate into the upper atmosphere → **auroras** (~100-300 km altitude). **Substorm injection** dumps fresh plasma sheet particles via reconnection. Particle precipitation rate determines auroral brightness.

question.question: Compute Larmor radius + E×B drift in ITER edge plasma
question.goal: Edge plasma B = 5 T, T_i = 100 eV, E_r = 30 kV/m radial electric field. Compute (a) r_L for thermal D⁺; (b) v_E; (c) Mach number; (d) parallel transit time across 5 m.

steps.prompt: Compute thermal v⊥ for 100 eV D⁺ (m = 3.34×10⁻²⁷ kg).
steps.reveal: v_th = √(2 × 1.6×10⁻¹⁷ / 3.34×10⁻²⁷) ≈ √(9.6×10⁹) ≈ **9.8×10⁴ m/s ≈ 100 km/s**. Often use v_th = √(k_B T/m) for 1D thermal speed.
r_L = (3.34×10⁻²⁷ × 9.8×10⁴) / (1.6×10⁻¹⁹ × 5) = 3.27×10⁻²² / 8×10⁻¹⁹ ≈ **4.1×10⁻⁴ m ≈ 0.4 mm**. Tiny compared to ITER's 2 m minor radius → magnetization holds for thermal ions.

steps.prompt: Compute v_E = E/B in m/s + compare to v_th.
steps.reveal: v_E = 30000/5 = **6000 m/s = 6 km/s**. Mach number M_E = v_E/v_th ≈ 6/100 = 0.06 — subsonic E×B rotation. Edge poloidal flow in real tokamaks can reach M ~ 0.1-0.3 driven by ∇p_i + neoclassical transport — important for L-H transition + edge transport barriers.

steps.prompt: Parallel transit time for v∥ = v_th across 5 m connection length.
steps.reveal: τ_∥ = L/v∥ ≈ 5/10⁵ = **5×10⁻⁵ s = 50 μs**. Compare to E×B rotation period for 1 m circuit: 1/6×10³ ≈ 170 μs. Compare to gyroperiod 2π/ω_c ≈ 2π × 3.34×10⁻²⁷/(1.6×10⁻¹⁹×5) ≈ 26 ns. Strong scale separation gyromotion ≪ transit ≪ E×B rotation — the adiabatic / drift expansion is excellent.

question.question: Why is the E × B drift independent of charge + mass?
options: From the drift formula v_d = (F×B)/(qB²) with F = qE: the charge cancels, giving v_E = (E×B)/B² independent of charge sign + magnitude. Physically: a positive ion accelerates in the +E direction, gains v∥E, then curves under v×B back the other way; the net guiding-center motion is sideways (perpendicular to both E + B) with the same speed regardless of mass — the cycloid orbits just have different sizes (r_L ∝ m). Electrons + ions drift **together**, so no current — only **transport**. This is fundamental to tokamak rotation (poloidal + toroidal flow shear), ionospheric convection (driven by solar-wind E field mapped down field lines), Hall thrusters (E×B confines electrons, accelerates ions axially), and magnetospheric plasma drift patterns. **Mass-dependent drifts** (grad-B, curvature, polarization, gravity) drive currents.
question.explanation: v_E = E×B/B² is independent of q + m because the q cancels with the qE force. Electrons + ions drift together → no current, only bulk transport. Drives tokamak rotation, ionospheric convection, Hall thrusters, magnetospheric circulation. Mass/charge-dependent drifts (∇B, curvature, polarization, g) drive currents instead.

hints: Plug F = qE into v_d = F×B/(qB²).
What does charge-independence imply for currents?
slides.workedSolution: Using v_d = F×B/(qB²) with F = qE: q cancels → v_E = E×B/B² depends only on field configuration. Both ion + electron drift identically (no current, just transport). Underlies tokamak rotation, ionospheric convection, Hall thrusters, magnetospheric drift. Charge/mass-dependent drifts (∇B, curvature, polarization, gravity) instead drive currents.

question.question: Designing a magnetic mirror confinement device
question.prompt: You're designing a magnetic mirror with central field B_min = 1 T + throat field B_max = 5 T (mirror ratio R_m = 5). For an isotropic Maxwellian distribution at T = 1 keV: (a) compute the loss-cone angle θ_lc; (b) estimate the fractional loss per bounce; (c) explain why this makes steady-state fusion confinement difficult vs a closed-field tokamak; (d) why do Van Allen belts trap particles for years despite being a mirror?

question.question: Write the first adiabatic invariant (magnetic moment).
question.hint: Perpendicular kinetic energy divided by magnetic field strength.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain how single-particle motion in magnetized plasma decomposes into gyromotion + guiding-center drifts + adiabatic invariants.
question.rubric: Mentions: Lorentz force F = qE + qv×B gives fast circular gyromotion at ω_c = qB/m with Larmor radius r_L = mv⊥/(qB); guiding center is the average position. Slow forces drive drifts: E×B drift (charge-independent, drives transport not current), grad-B + curvature + polarization + gravity drifts (charge-dependent, drive currents). Three adiabatic invariants — magnetic moment μ = mv⊥²/(2B) (gyro), longitudinal J = ∮mv∥ds (bounce), flux Φ (drift) — conserved when fields vary slowly. μ conservation gives mirror trapping: particles with sin²θ < B_min/B_max escape the loss cone; Van Allen belts (Explorer 1, 1958) trap radiation-belt particles for years. Concludes: this hierarchy — gyromotion ≪ bounce ≪ drift periods — underlies all magnetic confinement + space plasma physics + leads to gyrokinetics + drift theory.
